subject: botany_2
question_text: Name any two industrially important enzymes.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.49, printed question 142. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Two names, then two uses. Streptokinase is worth naming because its use is dramatic.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Two enzymes
steps.margin_note: Both names plus two spares. Four lines.
lines: AMYLASE and PECTINASE are two more.
steps.why: All four are made by microbes in fermentors, which is what makes them industrially available at all.
common_mistakes: Naming an enzyme from a plant. The question is about industrially produced ones.
Naming one enzyme. The question asks for two.

steps.label: What each is used for
steps.margin_note: At least two named uses, each matched to its enzyme.
lines: LIPASES are used in DETERGENT formulations, to
STREPTOKINASE, from Streptococcus, is used as a
CLOT BUSTER to remove clots from the blood vessels
PECTINASES and proteases are used to CLARIFY
steps.why: Each enzyme does industrially exactly what it does biologically — lipase digests fat, streptokinase dissolves fibrin — so the use follows from the name.
common_mistakes: Giving names with no uses. The uses are the second mark.
Saying streptokinase is used in detergents. It is a medical clot buster.
steps.memory_tip: Lipase for fat, streptokinase for clots, pectinase for juice.
